messages:
Maria Chen: FYI support escalated several customers seeing spikes of 401/500s during last night's maintenance window. Errors look auth-related, possibly key related. Attaching log excerpt.

Support Bot: Incident created INC-2026-0316-004. Affected customers: 5 accounts (internal IDs).

Jess Ortega: Acknowledged — jumping in. Which KMS rotation ran? cloud-kms or HSM rotation?

Samir Patel: It was cloud-kms automated rotation at 02:07 UTC. I saw a small subset of nodes failed to fetch the new wrapping key, so some token validation tried old key id. Quick log sample:

```
auth ERROR: token validation failed: key id 'rk-2026-03-16' not found
request_id=abc123 user=aCust
22:07:18Z node=node-17 fetch-key failed: 403
```

Jess Ortega: That matches the 401s. Are we sure this affected any plaintext customer data?

Ava Li: Security note: from initial review, this is an availability/auth issue — we have no evidence of data exfil. We still need to run a full audit to confirm scope. Audit logs retention is 90 days for control-plane events and 365 for customer audit exports.

Maria Chen: Support wants guidance on customer comms timeline — some customers have asked if they should be notified.

Ava Li: If we confirm no customer data was accessed improperly, this is an incident affecting availability; still recommend proactive outreach for impacted customers explaining cause and mitigations. For any confirmed unauthorized access we must notify within 72 hours per our policy.

Jess Ortega: Agreed. Plan: 1) Samir to finish forensic capture + list of impacted accounts by 12:30 UTC. 2) I will draft initial customer note (availability-focused) and post for review by 13:30. 3) Maria/Leo to coordinate CSM outreach.

Samir Patel: Running key reconciliation now. Repro steps for support/devs:
1. curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
2. Observe 401 with header X-Auth-Key: rk-2026-03 if key id mismatch
3. Check node logs: kubectl logs node-17 | grep "fetch-key"

Support Bot: Adding repro steps to the support ticket.

Jess Ortega: We should also check audit-log writes around rotation time for any failed key fetches or retries. Ava, can security pull those?

Ava Li: On it. I'll export control-plane audit logs from 02:00–02:30 UTC and look for key-service errors. Also enabling elevated retention snapshot for 30 days for this timeline.

Maria Chen: For Customers: do we want a short "we experienced auth failures during maintenance, services are restored, here's what we're doing" or something more detailed?

Leo (CSM): Keep it concise and non-technical for customers impacted. Include: timeline, impact (temporary auth failures), mitigations (fallback applied, no data loss observed), next steps (we're investigating and will update). Offer priority support channel.

Jess Ortega: Drafted initial note, posting below for quick review: 
"We experienced intermittent authentication errors affecting a small set of requests during a scheduled key rotation on March 16. We applied a fallback and restored normal service within ~20 minutes. We are running a full audit to confirm no customer data was exposed. If you experienced errors, please reply or open a support ticket and we'll prioritize investigation."

Ava Li: LGTM from security. Add a line about expected follow-up timeline: we'll provide a forensic summary within 72 hours or earlier.

Samir Patel: Mitigation completed: re-run key-sync across nodes and forced refresh. I also pushed a change to make key fetch retries more aggressive during rotation windows. Will open PR for postmortem remediation.

Oncall Bot: Update: incident status -> triaged, mitigation applied, assigned to eng-runtime for RCA.

Maria Chen: Thanks team. Action owners: Samir (forensic capture + PR), Jess (customer note + incident timeline), Ava (audit export + compliance check), Leo (CSM outreach). Please update this thread as you have new info.

Jess Ortega: Will post final affected-customer list and message variants (technical + customer) by 13:30 UTC.

Samir Patel: Forensics: initial list shows 5 accounts with transient errors; no signs of token replay or unauthorized API calls. Will confirm after log correlation.

Ava Li: If that holds, compliance: we document incident in tracker, no regulatory notification required beyond customer outreach. If anything changes we will follow breach notification policy.

Maria Chen: Perfect. Keep this thread for the updates. :thumbsup:
